3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: Symon Holl, Gus Manger and Lileas Graf were about to arrive at the White Room for our scheduled economy meeting. This was the room in the Maroon Palace where all important meetings were held.

4.speaker: Symon Holl
4.text: “My staff and I have comprehensively analyzed every aspect of--"

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: He was interrupted by a groan from one of the assistants by the door, both of whom were now visibly struggling to hold up the heavy projector.

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: He pointed below the painting of President Soll. The assistants placed the projector next to the table and installed a white screen on the wall.

8.speaker: Player
8.text: “What is our GDP and debt situation?”

9.speaker: Player
9.text: “What is our unemployment and inflation rate?”

10.speaker: Symon Holl
10.text: “Since economics is your forte, Mr. Rayne, it is possible that you might already be aware of the data. I can still explain the current economic situation in better detail.”

11.speaker: Symon Holl
11.text: “Mr. President? I'm about to explain some very serious data.”

14.speaker: Symon Holl
14.text: “I am very well and motivated, Mr. Rayne. It seems our ministers are feeling the same.”

15.speaker: Player
15.text: “What is the status of the recession?”

16.speaker: Symon Holl
16.text: “Our current GDP is 310 billion Sordish Ren and the national debt is 427 billion.”

17.speaker: Symon Holl
17.text: “The economy has been in a recession of about -6% in the past year. The average GDP has dropped from SR 15,454 per capita to SR 10,359 from 1951 to now.”

18.speaker: Symon Holl
18.text: “Unemployment has skyrocketed and is now at a staggering 16% and the inflation is at a relative high of 10%.”

19.speaker: Narrator
19.text: Symon scattered the paper stack in front of him in an orderly manner and took a final look at his notes before clearing his throat.

22.speaker: Player
22.text: “I have all the information needed. Let's move on to the economic strategy.”

25.speaker: Gus Manger
25.text: "Don't be an idiot, Lileas. What about the unemployment crisis the Greater Holsord and Gelsland regions are going through? These areas are our economic heartland.”

26.speaker: Lileas Graf
26.text: “Gus, do you really think that such an economically advanced area is more in need of investment than Agnland?”

28.speaker: Narrator
28.text: From the hallway, I heard Lileas Graf's voice. She was using the patient, almost motherly tone she often took in heated arguments.

29.speaker: Narrator
29.text: Symon Holl quickly stepped between the two ministers without looking at either of them. He cleared his throat.

32.speaker: Lileas Graf
32.text: “Just a disagreement in internal economic strategy, President Rayne.”

33.speaker: Gus Manger
33.text: “Not sure if I would call it just a disagreement, Lileas.”

36.speaker: Lileas Graf
36.text: “We've already begun restructuring local governments and introducing new safety measures. Off to a good start.”

37.speaker: Gus Manger
37.text: “It's looking good, sir. Although there seems to be a lot of work that requires attention.”

38.speaker: Player
38.text: “Just as expected. How is it going, Gus and Lileas?”

39.speaker: Lileas Graf
39.text: “Meanwhile, many cities in Agnland like Lenkurg or Arvory still don't have basic commodities delivered in time.”

41.speaker: Gus Manger
41.text: “Ms. Graf seeks to focus our economic development in a region where we can't reap the financial benefits.”

43.speaker: Symon Holl
43.text: “Yes. I will move forward with my presentation if no one objects?”

47.speaker: Player
47.text: “Good. I am confident in your abilities."

48.speaker: Player
48.text: “If there is anything you need help with, reach out to me.”

53.speaker: Player
53.text: "I can clearly see that. What was that discussion about?"

54.speaker: Gus Manger
54.text: “We were having a discussion about the infrastructure plans. If I may, I would like to talk to you about the-"

55.speaker: Symon Holl
55.text: “Thank you, Mr. President. Now I would like to show you the latest economic situation.”

56.speaker: Narrator
56.text: Symon started looking for his slides. He always carried documentation around with him.

57.speaker: Symon Holl
57.text: “Leave now. I mean, thank you and please leave now.”

58.speaker: Symon Holl
58.text: “First, I would like to conduct my economy presentation.”

60.speaker: Narrator
60.text: The assistants left the cabinet room. I was reminded that Symon had never quite had a way with people. But his facility with numbers had made him the most sought-after economic specialist in Sordland.

61.speaker: Lileas Graf
61.text: “A wise idea, if your main agenda is to make money instead of developing the region and serving the people.”

62.speaker: Gus Manger
62.text: “Sir, I have some very good construction companies willing to take government contracts in Greater Holsord and Gelsland.”

65.speaker: Lileas Graf
65.text: “Pardon me, Mr. President. I just want the best for the city of Arvory and the Agnland region in general."

66.speaker: Lileas Graf
66.text: “Of course. The argument is simple. Agnland is our weakest region both in terms of economic and social support.”

72.speaker: Symon Holl
72.text: “I have to say that I agree with both of them. Agnland is in need of investment, and we can improve Greater Holsord and Gelsland.”

74.speaker: Gus Manger
74.text: “This snake of a woman is the former mayor of Arvory, and Eric Niel is her successor. Her argument could be biased.”

75.speaker: Lileas Graf
75.text: “Gus, dear, my arguments are proven by simple economic data. Our poorest and least developed region is Agnland.”

76.speaker: Lileas Graf
76.text: “The facts are clear. But it seems to me that you'd rather resort to name-calling to push your agenda.”

77.speaker: Narrator
77.text: Lileas smiled and folded her hands primly.

78.speaker: Symon Holl
78.text: “I want to avoid this topic now since we will talk about it in the future. I would rather first fully brief you on our current economic situation.”

79.speaker: Gus Manger
79.text: “The figures are being skewed in Nargis to make it look like a developed region, for example. In truth, it is the poorest region of all.”

80.speaker: Symon Holl
80.text: “I would like to put a stop to this debate. We will discuss it all calmly and logically.”

81.speaker: Lileas Graf
81.text: “Symon, what happened to the new police station construction in Estord?”

82.speaker: Narrator
82.text: While going through his briefcase, he paused for a moment to answer.

83.speaker: Symon Holl
83.text: “It got stalled due to a government property boundary issue. I have been meaning to look at it.”

84.speaker: Lileas Graf
84.text: “I can take a look at that one. Estord needs all the security help it can get.”

85.speaker: Symon Holl
85.text: “Sure. More time for me to spend on analyses.”

86.speaker: Narrator
86.text: His eyes glittered when he finally found the slides he were looking for.

87.speaker: Gus Manger
87.text: “It's still hard to fathom that we lost nearly 150 billion in wealth. The past three years were tough.”

88.speaker: Lileas Graf
88.text: “Unemployment is increasing crime and drug use. We need to get people off the streets. The inflation isn't helping our average citizen either.”

89.speaker: Symon Holl
89.text: “This administration's success depends on our ability to stop the recession. The sooner we can reach GDP growth the better.”

91.speaker: Player
91.text: “I am interested in what Gus has to say.”

93.speaker: Gus Manger
93.text: “Sir, I have some very good construction companies willing to take government contracts in the Greater Holsord and Gelsland regions.”

94.speaker: Gus Manger
94.text: “This would boost the rural economy. I think it would be wise to pick investments that will go through these regions.”

96.speaker: Player
96.text: “No need to rush this, Gus. We will figure it out.”

97.speaker: Gus Manger
97.text: “This would boost the rural economy. I think it would be wise to pick investments that will go through these regions.”

98.speaker: Player
98.text: “I agree that the countryside needs investment.”

104.speaker: Player
104.text: “Lileas, what are your thoughts on this proposition?”

120.speaker: Symon Holl
120.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn01_EnT_Listened_Hub_QOL"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn01_EnT_Listened_Hub_UNEMP"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn01_EnT_Listened_Hub_GDP"] == true) == false

124.speaker: Symon Holl
124.text: “One of our main promises was to promote a planned economy to stop the recession. To be frank, I still don't think this was a good idea.”

126.speaker: Player
126.text: “Promote a planned economy as we promised.”

129.speaker: Symon Holl
129.text: “So, what will our general economic plan promote?”

130.speaker: Lileas Graf
130.text: “I still do not support it. Why promote the private sector when we have qualified state-owned enterprises?”

131.speaker: Gus Manger
131.text: “We shouldn't go back to Sollonomics. It is the reason for the recession.”

132.speaker: Lileas Graf
132.text: “I can't say that I agree with this.”

133.speaker: Gus Manger
133.text: “Not sure if we made the right decision here.”

134.speaker: Symon Holl
134.text: “Now that there is clarity on which direction we are heading. I will work on a good plan accordingly.”

139.speaker: Player
139.text: “What are the consequences of the free-market?”

142.speaker: Player
142.text: “What are the downsides of the planned economy?”

143.speaker: Symon Holl
143.text: “Choosing construction contractors, trade relations, tax reform and privatization initiatives would be some of them.”

144.speaker: Symon Holl
144.text: “There are not many but one could say that we are much more likely to be influenced by the world economy.”

145.speaker: Symon Holl
145.text: “The structural problems of Sollonomics were going to lead to a recession according to the predictions at the time anyway. Either way, even if we pick one of the doctrines, we retain the option to make economic choices on a case-by-case basis.”

146.speaker: Symon Holl
146.text: “It is clear that most of the state corporations and other government controlled systems are less efficient.”

147.speaker: Symon Holl
147.text: “Picking a construction company, trade relations, tax reform and welfare privatization or nationalization initiatives would be some of them.”

148.speaker: Lileas Graf
148.text: “Sticking to a solid planned economy strategy will be the right call. The five-year plans were fruitful in the past.”

149.speaker: Gus Manger
149.text: “It is important to think about this subject because the upswings of the world economy will reflect good on ours too.”

150.speaker: Lileas Graf
150.text: “That is, however, not recommended in my point of view. The last thing we need is a chaotic economic plan.”

151.speaker: Lileas Graf
151.text: “The government of Sordland and its institutions or corporations have a solid history of delivering.”

152.speaker: Gus Manger
152.text: “We must choose wisely and remember that the free-market economy in all forms is the future of the world.”

153.speaker: Narrator
153.text: Symon put forward a legal document outlining the possibilities with both economic doctrines listed. The cabinet members looked at me.

154.speaker: Symon Holl
154.text: “What are your final thoughts, Mr. President?”

155.speaker: Lileas Graf
155.text: “Self-sufficiency will help us in tough times.”

156.speaker: Gus Manger
156.text: “Because the lack of competition has made them inefficient.”

157.speaker: Player
157.text: “Critical institutions must remain in state control. We must be fully responsible in delivering services.”

158.speaker: Player
158.text: “We should look at opportunities like privatization to create financial resources.”

159.speaker: Player
159.text: “It is hard to fully agree or disagree with these options.”

160.speaker: Symon Holl
160.text: “A market economy doesn't mean privatization of every single institution. But either way, you make the choices.”

161.speaker: Symon Holl
161.text: “This is exactly my mentality. There are many possibilities that are waiting, like education or health privatization. It would be better to promote a market economy for these to have consistency with our plan.”

162.speaker: Symon Holl
162.text: “It's a difficult position to be in, Mr. President. But your final say is what counts. Remember, this is the overall strategic direction. Our ability to make individual economic decisions still remains.”

163.speaker: Narrator
163.text: Now that the economic direction was decided upon, the ministers dispersed for lunch at the Maroon Palace.

164.speaker: Narrator
164.text: Two assistants arrived first, carrying a heavy projector. They stood with it by the door, waiting for the ministers to enter.

165.speaker: Symon Holl
165.text: “We will get there, Gus. No rush.”

166.speaker: Gus Manger
166.text: “Especially about lifting people out of poverty. Certainly, a challenge.”

167.speaker: Lileas Graf
167.text: “I am feeling fairly confident about the current state of affairs.”

169.speaker: Lileas Graf
169.text: “Mr. Manger proposes that we should invest in already developed regions.”

170.speaker: Lileas Graf
170.text: “We should support the city of Arvory and its respected mayor.”

174.speaker: Player
174.text: “Would a free-market focus bring us stronger allies?”

175.speaker: Player
175.text: “Would a planned economy focus bring us stronger allies?”

176.speaker: Player
176.text: “We have to thank Soll and his planned economy for the boom. It clearly shows the success of the system.”

177.speaker: Symon Holl
177.text: “This concludes our meeting. At our next gathering we will talk about the upcoming infrastructure investment plan.”

178.speaker: Lileas Graf
178.text: “Diplomatically, it would make United Contana look at our country in a more positive light. They are proponents of the planned economy.”

179.speaker: Gus Manger
179.text: “It would make Arcasia look at our country in a more positive light. They are proponents of the free-market economy.”

180.speaker: Symon Holl
180.text: “The influence Arcasia has on the world economy is extensive. Our economic strategy should be based on internal reasoning though.”

181.speaker: Symon Holl
181.text: “Whatever that's worth. The influence Arcasia has on the world economy is extensive. Our economic strategy should be based on internal reasoning, though.”

182.speaker: Player
182.text: “Let's finish what Alphonso started with the capitalist free-market reforms. His path was going to enrich Sordland.”

183.speaker: Lileas Graf
183.text: “Precisely the reason why we should stick to the old system. State planning and regulation both showed great success in the 30s.”

184.speaker: Gus Manger
184.text: “History must note that the reason for the recession was because Ewald Alphonso was betrayed by his party.”

185.speaker: Lileas Graf
185.text: “The recession was the direct result of his free-market reforms.”

186.speaker: Gus Manger
186.text: “Only for a limited time, until even Tarquin Soll himself discovered the limits of the system. The slowdown began during his rule, remember?”

189.speaker: Lileas Graf
189.text: “Yes... And when the global economy crashes, we go down with it.”

220.speaker: Gus Manger
220.text: “Finally something we can both agree on, Lileas.”

221.speaker: Lileas Graf
221.text: “That is not true, there was plenty of time for him to do it. If you can't make change happen in two years then you are at fault.”

225.speaker: Player
225.text: “Promote a free-market economy as we promised.”

230.speaker: Symon Holl
230.text: “What would you like to know about the current economic situation?”

231.speaker: Narrator
231.text: The Recession of '51 put enormous pressure on the economy, resulting in the collapse of the value of our currency. The entire situation was a significant cause of concern for our administration.

232.speaker: Symon Holl
232.text: “There have been some developments about the Sordish Ren losing further value today. We have been trying to stabilize it with the Central Bank.”

235.speaker: Gus Manger
235.text: “Business leaders are requesting better logistical links in order to contribute to the economy more.”

236.speaker: Player
236.text: “A market economy doesn't require as much guidance and could help us attract foreign capital.”

237.speaker: Symon Holl
237.text: “Especially from Arcasia. President Walker is always interested in expanding the economic zone of ATO. We could secure lucrative investments from capitalist countries.”

238.speaker: Narrator
238.text: Lileas, my Interior Minister, strode in. She was clad in shades of brown and beige, the only spot of color a bright yellow Dastnurist cross on her necklace. Gus followed close behind.

239.speaker: Narrator
239.text: Gus curled his hands into fists. The Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development's temper hadn't changed since his days in the Alphonso administration, but neither had his reputation for getting things done. His far-reaching network of connections was unlike any other.

251.speaker: Symon Holl
251.text: “One of our main promises was to promote a free-market economy to stop the recession. To be frank, I believe it is the only way out of the recession.”

252.speaker: Lileas Graf
252.text: “There is another important factor which has a direct impact on our economy. Superpowers.”

259.speaker: Lileas Graf
259.text: “We might have won the election but I am still against aligning ourselves with the superpowers.”

260.speaker: Lileas Graf
260.text: “We might have won the election, but I am still against aligning ourselves with any superpowers.”

261.speaker: Lileas Graf
261.text: “I want you to reconsider your promise to align with Arcasia.”

262.speaker: Lileas Graf
262.text: “We have done well not aligning ourselves with any one of them.”

263.speaker: Lileas Graf
263.text: “We must be very cautious. There are schemes being devised about Sordland. We can not give in to their wants now or in the future. Otherwise our country will turn into a pawn.”

264.speaker: Player
264.text: “Don't worry. I won't let United Contana control Sordland.”

265.speaker: Player
265.text: “I have made a promise to the people of Sordland. I won't back down.”

266.speaker: Lileas Graf
266.text: “We must be very cautious. There are schemes being devised about Sordland. We can not give in to their wants now or in the future. Otherwise our country will turn into a pawn.”

267.speaker: Lileas Graf
267.text: “I want you to reconsider your promise to align with United Contana.”

268.speaker: Lileas Graf
268.text: “We must be very cautious. There are schemes being devised about Sordland. We can not give in to their wants now or in the future. Otherwise our country will turn into a pawn.”

269.speaker: Player
269.text: “There is a revolution that was started by United Contana. A permanent revolution. And Sordland must be part of it.”

270.speaker: Gus Manger
270.text: “I hope we can show and not tell.”

271.speaker: Gus Manger
271.text: “I must also insist. Nothing good will come out of siding with United Contana. Aligning with them may make us adversaries to Arcasia, a much more influential nation in my view.”

272.speaker: Player
272.text: “You may be right. Let's see what the future brings.”

273.speaker: Gus Manger
273.text: “We will see how long it will last.”

275.speaker: Gus Manger
275.text: “I am also with Lileas on this one. Nothing good will come out of siding with United Contana. Aligning with them may make us adversaries to Arcasia, a much more influential nation in my view.”

276.speaker: Lileas Graf
276.text: “Although not for the same reasons, that's two things we are agreeing on today, Gus.”

278.speaker: Symon Holl
278.text: “Let's not get ahead of ourselves. Minister Wisci will be in charge of informing you on those types of foreign policy decisions. We must first decide on our internal economic plan.”

279.speaker: Lileas Graf
279.text: “Although not for the same reasons, that's two things we are agreeing on today, Gus.”

280.speaker: Player
280.text: “I have made a promise to the people of Sordland. I won't back down.”

281.speaker: Player
281.text: “Don't worry. I won't let Arcasia control Sordland.”

282.speaker: Player
282.text: “Entering the sphere of Arcasia will help boost our economy in many ways. They are wealthy and influential.”

283.speaker: Gus Manger
283.text: “Control? No, Mr. President, it's simply a partnership. And a very valuable one at that.”

284.speaker: Lileas Graf
284.text: “When the time comes, I hope you will make the right decision. For our own good.”

285.speaker: Gus Manger
285.text: “Exactly. We have made a promise. People want to trust their President. What kind of an example we would set for the future generations if we were to back down on our promises?”

286.speaker: Gus Manger
286.text: “Mr. President. We have made a promise. People want to trust their President. What kind of an example we would set for future generations if we were to back down on our promises?”

287.speaker: Gus Manger
287.text: “Exactly. I like to think of it as a very valuable partnership. With the deals we will get by aligning ourselves with a strong country like Arcasia, recession would surely end in no time.”

289.speaker: Player
289.text: “You may be right. Let's see what the future brings.”

290.speaker: Lileas Graf
290.text: “I know you have campaigned for this in the party a long time, Gus.”

291.speaker: Lileas Graf
291.text: “Future generations would be thankful everyday for making the right decision when Sordland is the only nation in the region that is not a puppet.”

292.speaker: Gus Manger
292.text: “Also, in my opinion, aligning with a powerful country like Arcasia was an excellent decision.”

293.speaker: Lileas Graf
293.text: “Mr. President. This is exactly what being controlled looks like. Voluntarily or involuntarily.”

294.speaker: Narrator
294.text: Gus eyed Lileas with distrust but didn't say anything.

295.speaker: Lileas Graf
295.text: “Valuable for Arcasia maybe. Not for Sordland.”

298.speaker: Player
298.text: “Time will show if staying neutral will work out.”

299.speaker: Player
299.text: “Sordland will not be controlled by any nations.”

300.speaker: Player
300.text: “Exactly. Soll was right all along with his policies.”

302.speaker: Lileas Graf
302.text: “I am glad we are on the same page.”

304.speaker: Lileas Graf
304.text: “Precisely my point. We will stand strong and show an example to the world.”

305.speaker: Player
305.text: “I still haven't decided if they wish to come with a deal.”

306.speaker: Lileas Graf
306.text: “A deal that they would surely come out with more profit while our people suffered.”

307.speaker: Gus Manger
307.text: “We don't know that. We should wait and see. With the deals we could get by aligning ourselves with a strong country like Arcasia, recession would surely end in no time.”

308.speaker: Lileas Graf
308.text: “We must make it work to protect our country and our values. There is no other way.”

309.speaker: Gus Manger
309.text: “We need to be open to other possibilities. Arcasia is a strong country and If we end up in their sphere, Sordland would increase its influence in the world.”

310.speaker: Gus Manger
310.text: “The deals we would get would surely bring us out of recession.”

312.speaker: Symon Holl
312.text: “Economically speaking, we are much closer to Arcasia than United Contana, so a decision to align with the west makes more sense.”

313.speaker: Symon Holl
313.text: “Economically speaking, we aren't as tied to United Contana as we are to Arcasia, so a decision to align with the east is much more difficult to accomplish.”

314.speaker: Symon Holl
314.text: “Economically speaking, an isolationist policy overall could only work if we were to reap the benefits of both spheres and their rivalry. This is very dangerous to attempt but still possible.”

315.speaker: Player
315.text: “The more of the economy we control, the better we can manage the recession.”

316.speaker: Player
316.text: “Economic systems without regulation are bound to fail.”

317.speaker: Player
317.text: “Humanity in the 20th century is thriving because of the rule of supply and demand.”

318.speaker: Gus Manger
318.text: “From taxes to the standard of goods, there are many elements that regulate all aspects of this system.”

319.speaker: Lileas Graf
319.text: “But is it enough? I doubt it. If we can manage to plan more aspects of the economy, our chances of success would increase with a talented team like ours.”

320.speaker: Symon Holl
320.text: “Obviously there is some regulation in all of the existing systems, otherwise it would be anarchy. Nobody wants a chaotic society.”

321.speaker: Lileas Graf
321.text: “One way to be remembered positively is to cause a recession and leave a few bills behind.”

322.speaker: Gus Manger
322.text: “Say what you will about Alphonso, without his attempts our current coffers would be empty and the recession would be a depression.”

323.speaker: Symon Holl
323.text: “That is a fair argument to be made. But if we reduce the freedom of people in the market place in general, it would hinder our innovation and dynamism in the supply and demand equation.”

324.speaker: Lileas Graf
324.text: “Integrating heavily in a market economy would work if we had extensive means of production. Our industry is lacking.”

325.speaker: Gus Manger
325.text: “Sordland has the potential to do so as well. Why don't we take our potential seriously?”

326.speaker: Symon Holl
326.text: “Agreed. Look at how quickly Lespia and Arcasia have increased their prosperity by embracing these basic principles.”

333.speaker: Symon Holl
333.text: “As you can see, the situation is alarming, but not everything is negative. The extensive privatization program of Alphonso and key foreign direct investments left us a large budget surplus which we can use to stabilize the crisis.”

334.speaker: Symon Holl
334.text: “The primary subject we need to settle on is what general path we will take in our term. Sollonomics-based nationalization happened in the '30s and Alphonso's privatization began during the end of the '40s. What will our administration focus on?”

335.speaker: Narrator
335.text: Symon pulled a silk handkerchief out of his pocket and briefly wiped his glasses.

346.speaker: Gus Manger
346.text: “We should attract more foreign direct investment. Mr. President, we saved the country from a full-on depression in 1952 and 1953 by signing lucrative trade deals with nations such as Rizia, Lespia, and Qinal.”

347.speaker: Narrator
347.text: Lileas had a sip of water from her glass.

349.speaker: Player
349.text: “No need for questions. I am well aware of the details. Let's move on to our strategy.”
349.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn01_EnT_Listened_Hub_QOL"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn01_EnT_Listened_Hub_UNEMP"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn01_EnT_Listened_Hub_GDP"] == true) == false

351.speaker: Player
351.text: "You already know what we're going to do."
